findings.summary: Nested destructuring is explained only as a hazard, with no safe pattern, so the learner is left without the fix.
findings.evidence: "Nested { address: { city } } throws if address is undefined"
findings.fix: Add a one-line fix such as "Default the parent: { address: { city } = {} } = user" or "use user.address?.city".

findings.summary: The mistakes list gives two bare fragments with no consequence or fix, so a skimming learner cannot tell what goes wrong.
findings.evidence: "map only for side effects: use forEach" and "reduce callback that forgets to return acc"
findings.fix: Write each as a full one-line rule: "Using map only for side effects builds a throwaway array; use forEach" and "Forgetting to return acc makes the next step see undefined".

findings.summary: One bullet packs three separate ideas about module behaviour.
findings.evidence: "Modules run once, are cached, and are strict mode"
findings.fix: Split into three bullets: runs once, cached, always strict mode.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "destructure").
findings.evidence: Destructure: const { a, b = 1, ...rest } = obj; const [x, , z] = arr
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The Safe Access and Pipeline section opens with code before any idea is stated, and the code lines carry no gloss.
findings.fix: Put the one-line ideas first ("?. short-circuits, ?? falls back", "filter, then map, then reduce") and then show the code, or add a short comment to each code line.
